A.explanation: 10 K is a temperature of $10 \text{ K}$, where kelvin is an SI base unit, so it is a valid measurement.

B.explanation: Since $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$, $\text{J N}^{-1} \text{m}^{-1}$ cancels to $(\text{N m})/(\text{N m}) = 1$ with no unit left, so it cannot be a measurement with a unit.

C.explanation: Since $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2}$, $\text{Pa m}^{3} \text{N}^{-1}$ simplifies to $\text{m}$, a length, so it is a valid measurement.

D.explanation: Since $1 \text{ T} = 1 \text{ N A}^{-1} \text{m}^{-1}$, $\text{T m}$ simplifies to $\text{N A}^{-1}$ which has dimensions, so it could be a physical quantity.

hints: Look at the unit combinations in $11 \text{ J N}^{-1} \text{m}^{-1}$ and $17 \text{ Pa m}^{3} \text{N}^{-1}$ - a valid measurement must leave a unit with dimensions.
Recall the derived-unit expansions $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$ for energy and $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2}$ for pressure.
Simplify each product and quotient of units to see which one cancels completely to the number 1 and which ones leave $\text{K}$, $\text{m}$ or $\text{N A}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: A measurement of a physical quantity needs a numerical magnitude together with a unit that has dimensions. Check each option by reducing named units to simpler units.
Option A is $10 \text{ K}$. Kelvin $\text{K}$ is the SI base unit of temperature, so this is valid.

Expand option B using $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$: $\text{J N}^{-1} \text{m}^{-1} = (\text{N m}) \times \text{N}^{-1} \times \text{m}^{-1} = 1$. The newtons cancel and the metres cancel, leaving a pure number $11$ with no unit.

Expand option C using $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2}$: $\text{Pa m}^{3} \text{N}^{-1} = (\text{N m}^{-2})(\text{m}^{3})(\text{N}^{-1}) = \text{m}$. This is the unit of length, so $17 \text{ Pa m}^{3} \text{N}^{-1}$ could measure a length.

Expand option D using $1 \text{ T} = 1 \text{ N A}^{-1} \text{m}^{-1}$: $\text{T m} = (\text{N A}^{-1} \text{m}^{-1})(\text{m}) = \text{N A}^{-1}$. This still has dimensions of force per current, so it could be a physical quantity. Only the B combination leaves no unit. This is option B.
